page: Microsoft Azure FX2mds_v2 is a memory-intensive virtual machine belonging to the FXmdsv2 family. It features 2 vCPUs mapped to 1 physical Intel Xeon 8573C core with hyper-threading running at a dedicated clock speed of 4.2 GHz. The server is equipped with 42.0 GB of RAM, yielding a high memory-to-core ratio of 21.0 GB per core. It includes 118 GB of local NVMe SSD storage and is premium storage capable. The architecture is x86_64, running on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor.

Benchmark data reveals strong single-threaded performance, with Geekbench single-core scores reaching the top tier and single-threaded gzip compression and bzip3 decompression performing strongly. However, multi-core and parallelized performance is limited due to the 2-vCPU hardware constraint, as evidenced by poor multi-core stress-ng and weak Geekbench multi-core scores. Memory bandwidth also exhibits constraints, with large-block read and write benchmarks registering in the poor and weak categories, respectively.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, this instance offers a specialized resource density, providing a large memory footprint relative to its low vCPU count, which is advantageous for memory-bound workloads that do not require massive parallel processing. It is suited for memory-intensive applications with low parallel compute requirements, such as small-scale caching layers, lightweight database operations, single-threaded data processing, and text processing tasks.
